title: SaaS Revenue Leakage: How to Identify Revenue Leaks in B2B SaaS
description: How to identify revenue leaks in a B2B SaaS business — trial conversion, activation, churn, failed payments, and expansion — without hiring more analysts.
keywords: how to identify revenue leaks in b2b saas

faq.q: How do I identify revenue leaks in my B2B SaaS business?
faq.a: Measure trial-to-paid conversion, time-to-first-value, involuntary churn from failed cards, expansion ask rate, and discount/refund drag. Estimate monthly dollars per gap and fix the largest operational leak first.

faq.q: How can I identify revenue leakage in my SaaS business without hiring more analysts?
faq.a: Use Stripe (or your processor), product analytics, and CRM exports plus five structured questions. Rough ranges are enough to prioritize — you do not need a dedicated analytics hire for a first pass.

faq.q: Where do SaaS companies leak the most revenue?
faq.a: Typically trial-to-paid conversion, early churn before activation, and involuntary churn from failed card charges.

faq.q: What is a good SaaS trial conversion rate?
faq.a: Varies by model; self-serve often targets 10–25% trial-to-paid. Below 5% with healthy signups usually signals a leak.

blocks.text: SaaS revenue leakage rarely shows up as one broken metric. It is usually a stack: trials that never activate, cards that fail silently, and customers who would upgrade but never see the right plan.
How to identify revenue leaks in B2B SaaS

Start with five measurements you can pull without a dedicated analyst: trial-to-paid rate, days to first value, share of churn that is involuntary (failed cards), expansion ask rate on healthy accounts, and promo/refund drag. Put a monthly dollar range on each, then fix the largest operational gap — often [failed payment recovery](/guides/failed-payment-recovery) or onboarding — before buying more traffic.

items: Trial signup without onboarding to first value
Pricing page mismatch vs actual buyer persona
Monthly churn above 5–7% without save flows
Failed payments with no Smart Retries or dunning
